candidates.title: The Nursery: Floorplan, CARISTA
candidates.summary: Public Records puts its Sunday daytime series in The Nursery, the open-air plant-nursery yard on the Gowanus campus. This one is Floorplan (Robert Hood's gospel-house project) alongside Dutch selector Carista, starting at 3pm. Tickets via Dice through the Public Records calendar.
candidates.fit: Outdoor daytime dancing in a small yard with the best sound system in Brooklyn is exactly the register of the BQE day party he loved, and Floorplan is the kind of booking you have to actually follow the scene to catch.

candidates.title: Elsewhere x h0l0: not without friends — Luke Alessi, William Kiss + more
candidates.summary: Elsewhere takes its programming off-site to h0l0, the tiny unmarked Ridgewood club, for a 'not without friends' night led by Luke Alessi with William Kiss and guests. Doors 10pm, tickets through Eventbrite via the Elsewhere calendar.
candidates.fit: Small, unmarked room, melodic-leaning house, no marketing budget — this is the 'you had to know someone' end of the scene he keeps asking for, and Alessi sits right next to the Anjunadeep/melodic lane in his library.

candidates.title: Dusky, dj poolboi (open to close), Rae Sada, shimmer
candidates.summary: Full-venue club night at Elsewhere with UK deep-house duo Dusky headlining, dj poolboi playing open to close in a second room, plus Rae Sada and shimmer. Doors 10:30pm, tickets via Eventbrite through the Elsewhere calendar.
candidates.fit: Dusky are the deep/melodic UK house end of what he already listens to, and Elsewhere's multi-room setup means he can move a group of three between rooms instead of standing in one crowd all night.

candidates.title: Mister Sunday: Eamon Harkin and Justin Carter
candidates.summary: The long-running Mister Sunday outdoor party in the Nowadays yard, with founders Eamon Harkin and Justin Carter splitting the booth — Justin 3pm to 6pm, Eamon 6pm to 8pm. Listed 3pm to 9pm at 56-06 Cooper Ave in Ridgewood.
candidates.fit: One of the last warm Sundays of the year, outdoors, in a yard, with a crowd that is there for the records and not the photos — the closest thing the city has to his BQE day-party memory, and early enough that he is home at a reasonable hour.

candidates.title: Kruder & Dorfmeister
candidates.summary: The Vienna downtempo duo Kruder & Dorfmeister are listed on the Brooklyn Steel calendar for Thursday October 1, 2026, with an 8pm start. Brooklyn Steel is the 1,800-capacity Greenpoint room; tickets are sold through AXS and the Bowery Presents.
candidates.fit: A Thursday-night German-language-scene act he would never see otherwise, in a room built for sound rather than spectacle — and it is over early enough for a dad on a weeknight.

candidates.title: Circoloco NYC (Halloween weekend, closing nights)
candidates.address: Brooklyn Navy Yard, Building 293, Assembly Rd
candidates.summary: Circoloco takes over Brooklyn Storehouse for two Halloween nights, October 30 and 31, with &ME, Rampa, Dixon, ANOTR, Mochakk, Seth Troxler, Carlita, Jimi Jules, Konstantin, Beltran and more across the Navy Yard warehouse. Listings note Brooklyn Storehouse is closing after these shows, so these are the venue's final nights.
candidates.fit: This is his once-or-twice-a-year big warehouse night: Keinemusik's Rampa and &ME plus Dixon is the Berlin melodic-house axis he actually listens to, it is a walk-ish ride from Fort Greene, and it is the last thing to ever happen in that building. Book now.

candidates.title: Titonton Duvanté, Shawn Dub / Mike Servito, JADALAREIGN / kels
candidates.summary: Saturday night across all three Public Records rooms: Titonton Duvanté and Shawn Dub in the Sound Room, Mike Servito and JADALAREIGN in the Atrium, kels Upstairs. Doors 11pm, tickets via Dice from the Public Records calendar.
candidates.fit: Sound Room is a couple hundred people and the best-sounding club in Brooklyn; Servito is a proper DJ's DJ. Good Saturday call when he wants records and not a headliner.

candidates.title: Perreito
candidates.summary: Perreito is a reggaeton and perreo party on the Elsewhere rooftop, starting 6pm on Saturday October 3. Tickets via Eventbrite through the Elsewhere calendar.
candidates.fit: Reggaeton outdoors at golden hour on one of the last rooftop weekends of the year — his Bad Bunny/Daddy Yankee lane, and it starts early enough to still be a normal evening.

candidates.title: BKG: Boydell, Sasababy, Ladler
candidates.summary: Thursday club night in Zone One, Elsewhere's smaller back room, with Boydell headlining plus Sasababy and Ladler. Doors 10:30pm; tickets via Eventbrite through the Elsewhere calendar.
candidates.fit: Thursday is his weeknight slot and Zone One is a genuinely small room — this is a cheap, low-commitment way to get one or two of the guys out to hear actual house music on a school night.

candidates.title: Disco Tehran Anniversary Party
candidates.summary: Disco Tehran, the Iranian-diaspora global-disco collective, marks its anniversary with a Sunday afternoon party on the Elsewhere rooftop starting at 4pm. Tickets via Eventbrite through the Elsewhere calendar.
candidates.fit: Community-run, dress-up-friendly, live-band-and-DJ global disco in daylight — the kind of scene party with no marketing budget he keeps saying he wants, and an easy sell for a date-night-adjacent Sunday with his wife.

candidates.title: Ahmed Spins
candidates.price_text: from about $38 on Dice
candidates.summary: South African Afro-house and amapiano producer Ahmed Spins is listed for Knockdown Center on Saturday October 24, 2026, with Dice showing tickets from roughly $38. Knockdown is the Maspeth warehouse complex with a main hall and back rooms.
candidates.fit: This is the one booking that lands squarely in his current Afro-house and amapiano phase, in a warehouse rather than a Manhattan bottle-service room. Worth grabbing tickets early.

candidates.title: The Nursery: Frank & Tony, Roman Flügel
candidates.summary: Sunday daytime in the open-air Nursery at Public Records with Frank & Tony (Scissor & Thread) and German house institution Roman Flügel, from 3pm. Tickets via Dice from the Public Records calendar.
candidates.fit: Roman Flügel is thirty years of German electronic music in one booth, playing outdoors in Gowanus on a Sunday afternoon. Deep-scene German credential plus daytime — both boxes.

candidates.title: Mark Broom, Julia Govor / Blue Hour, Neel / Yasmeenah
candidates.summary: Halloween-weekend Friday across all three Public Records rooms: Mark Broom and Julia Govor in the Sound Room, Blue Hour and Neel in the Atrium, Yasmeenah Upstairs. Doors 11pm, tickets via Dice.
candidates.fit: Proper Berlin-facing techno on a serious sound system in a room he can actually cross in ten steps — the small-room alternative if Circoloco the same night feels like too much.

candidates.title: Hearts & Diamonds: Midnight Magic [Live] with Three of Hearts
candidates.summary: Brooklyn disco band Midnight Magic play live in the Public Records Sound Room with DJs Three of Hearts (Rok One, Andi, Danny White) on Thursday October 15 at 8pm. Tickets via Dice from the Public Records calendar.
candidates.fit: A Thursday date night: live disco band in a 200-capacity listening room, dinner in the Atrium first. Dressed-up dancing without a club queue.

candidates.title: The Atrium: Soul Summit All Day Long
candidates.summary: Soul Summit, the Fort Greene Park house-music institution, takes over the Public Records Atrium all day from 4pm on Sunday October 18. Tickets via Dice from the Public Records calendar.
candidates.fit: Soul Summit is literally his front-yard party moved indoors for the fall — the most Fort Greene booking on this list, and a Sunday afternoon so it costs him nothing socially.

candidates.title: Dope Jams Halloween Ball
candidates.summary: The long-running Dope Jams crew throw their Halloween Ball across the Sound Room, Atrium and Upstairs at Public Records on October 31, doors 11pm. Tickets via Dice.
candidates.fit: Costume night thrown by one of the most stubbornly underground record-store crews in the city. He dressed up for Rocky Horror and for ABBA night; this is the dance-music version.

candidates.title: Franc Moody (DJ set), Cody Currie open to close
candidates.summary: Full-venue Friday at Elsewhere with a Franc Moody DJ set and Cody Currie playing open to close in the second room. Doors 10:30pm, tickets via Eventbrite through the Elsewhere calendar.
candidates.fit: Live-band-electronic and disco-house — the Polo & Pan / Franc Moody corner of his taste — with an open-to-close set in the other room for when he wants one DJ to actually build something.

candidates.title: DURATIONS Festival 2026
candidates.time_text: evenings from 6–7pm, plus late club nights and 11am sessions
candidates.summary: Public Records runs its week-long DURATIONS festival November 9 to 15, with William Basinski over three nights, Suzanne Ciani, a buttechno/Matana Roberts/Klein night, a Dasha Rush and Blue Hour club night on November 13, talks Upstairs and a farm dinner. Individual tickets and passes via Dice.
candidates.fit: A full week of deep-listening and experimental programming in his favorite sound room, with a proper techno night on the Friday. The kind of thing that sells out to people who already know about it, so worth booking in advance.

candidates.title: Bound: Blackout
candidates.summary: Bound, the New York hard-techno and industrial party founded by Katie Rex, brings its Blackout edition to Basement NY on October 30, 2026, with a STUDIO room takeover hosted by San Francisco's Squish. Basement is at 52-19 Flushing Ave in Maspeth.
candidates.fit: Basement is the closest New York gets to a Berlin club — no phones energy, brutal sound, no marketing. Right lane if he wants the hard end rather than the melodic end for Halloween weekend.

candidates.title: KETTAMA
candidates.summary: Irish house producer KETTAMA is listed for a 21+ show at Knockdown Center on Friday October 9, 2026 at 10pm. Knockdown is the Maspeth warehouse; primary tickets are normally sold through Dice or the venue site.
candidates.fit: Big, loud, melodic-adjacent rave house in a warehouse — the format he already knows he likes from the Kx5 night, at a fraction of the scale. Confirm the date on Knockdown's own page before he commits.

candidates.title: Diva Diva: PAURRO & Kiernan Laveaux, Saia & e-Lite, performance by Willow Pill
candidates.summary: Sunday afternoon Atrium party from 4pm with DJs PAURRO and Kiernan Laveaux, Saia and e-Lite, plus a live performance from Willow Pill. Tickets via Dice from the Public Records calendar.
candidates.fit: Daytime dancing with a drag performance built in — the same combination he liked at Phoenix, but on a Sunday afternoon in Gowanus instead of a late night in the East Village.

candidates.title: Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit (plus Kayla Harrison vs Amanda Nunes)
candidates.summary: UFC's annual Madison Square Garden night, Saturday November 14. Two title fights on top: interim heavyweight champ Ciryl Gane vs Josh Hokit, and Kayla Harrison defending the women's bantamweight belt against Amanda Nunes, plus Caio Borralho, Kevin Holland, Stephen Thompson and Jim Miller on the card. Public on-sale was Friday September 25 through Ticketmaster (event 3B00652EC2504689); UFC also sells VIP packages separately at ufcvip.com. I did not see face-value price tiers on the UFC page, so treat price as unconfirmed.
candidates.fit: This is the one big spectacle fight night of the fall in his city, and he trains Muay Thai and teaches Krav Maga, so a Garden card is his crew's night out. It is inside the radar window and tickets only went on sale three days ago, so buying now is the whole point.

candidates.title: Knicks home opener vs Philadelphia 76ers — championship ring night and banner raising
candidates.summary: The Knicks open their title defense at the Garden on Tuesday October 20 against LeBron James and the 76ers, and get their championship rings and raise the franchise's first banner before tip. Reported by ABC7 New York and Yahoo Sports off the NBA's August schedule release; I could not load MSG's own calendar to confirm tip time or price.
candidates.fit: He spent last spring watching the playoff run in bars with the guys. This is the payoff night for that, and a ring ceremony is the rare regular-season game worth paying for. It is a Tuesday, which only works because it is genuinely exceptional — book it now, it will not get cheaper.

candidates.title: UFC 333: Volkanovski vs Evloev (afternoon card from Abu Dhabi)
candidates.summary: Alexander Volkanovski vs Movsar Evloev headlines UFC 333 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on Saturday October 24, with the main card starting at 2pm New York time. Confirmed on UFC's own events schedule. This is a screen event, not a ticketed NYC one — I was not able to verify any specific Brooklyn bar hosting it.
candidates.fit: A 2pm main card is the only kind of pay-per-view that actually works for a dad: you watch a featherweight title fight with the guys over beers in the afternoon and are still home for dinner. Pick a bar with sound on and claim a table early.

candidates.title: UFC 332: Silva vs Wang (Saturday night card)
candidates.summary: UFC 332 runs Saturday October 3 from the Delta Center in Salt Lake City, flyweight title on the line between Natalia Silva and Wang Cong, main card 8pm New York time on Paramount+. Confirmed on UFC's events page. Again, a screen event — no NYC watch party was verified for this one.
candidates.fit: It is the only live fight content inside this week's window. Worth knowing about if the Saturday plan collapses, but it is not a card worth building a night around for someone who has a Garden show to save his money for in November.

candidates.title: Zum Schneider Oktoberfest — "Munich on the East River" (closing weekend)
candidates.time_text: Friday runs as one session, 5pm to 10pm
candidates.price_text: general seating $25 ($35 Saturdays), reserved $35 ($45 Saturdays), VIP table $110, rooftop biergarten $15
candidates.summary: Zum Schneider, the old East Village Bavarian institution, runs its Oktoberfest at Franklin Point on the Greenpoint waterfront from Sept 25 through Oct 4, 2026, in a Wiesn-style beer hall plus a rooftop biergarten over the East River. Liter mugs of festbier, Bavarian food, live oompah from Mösl Franzi, and traditional games. Sessions are ticketed in advance with standing and table tiers.
candidates.fit: This is the Oktoberfest that is actually German rather than a frat party, which is exactly the distinction he cares about, and the closing weekend lands on German Unity Day, Oct 3. Liter steins and a brass band on the Greenpoint waterfront is a clean guys' plan that he can book instead of texting around.

candidates.title: Meat Asia Asian BBQ pop-up at Strong Rope Red Hook
candidates.time_text: Taproom hours; pop-up serves through the afternoon and evening
candidates.price_text: No cover; pay per plate at the pop-up, beers on top
candidates.summary: Strong Rope's Red Hook taproom hosts the Meat Asia pop-up on Saturday Oct 3, serving Asian BBQ alongside Strong Rope's all-New-York-ingredient beers. It is a walk-in taproom situation, no tickets, tables can be reserved through the brewery.
candidates.fit: Strong Rope in Red Hook on a sunny day is already one of his favorite things, and this turns it into an actual plan with food worth showing up for instead of a generic hang. Low effort, good for two or three friends, done before dinner.

candidates.title: Black Forest Brooklyn Oktoberfest, Saturday session
candidates.price_text: Reported as $15 entry, $50 unlimited beer — secondary source, confirm before you go
candidates.summary: Black Forest Brooklyn's 12th annual Oktoberfest runs six weekends, Sept 19/20 through Oct 24/25, at both the Fort Greene and Smith Street rooms. Saturdays bring live German music, liter steins of Hofbräu Oktoberfest, German food, stein-holding competitions and costumes.
candidates.fit: It is a ten-minute walk from his door and it is a real German room, not a beer-tent gimmick, and the stein-holding contest gives him something to actually do rather than stand around. Oct 3 is German Unity Day, which makes it the right Saturday.

candidates.title: Red Hook Lobster Pound truck at Strong Rope Brewery
candidates.price_text: Free to enter; lobster rolls and beer priced à la carte
candidates.summary: The Red Hook Lobster Pound truck parks at Strong Rope's Red Hook taproom on Sunday Oct 4, serving lobster rolls while the brewery pours its New York-grown beers. Walk-in, no tickets.
candidates.fit: A Sunday-daytime Red Hook run works with a one-year-old: stroller-friendly streets, a taproom that is not a nightclub, waterfront to walk after, and he is back well before nap collapse. It is also a place he already likes, so no gamble.

candidates.title: RAW WINE New York 2026
candidates.time_text: Daytime tasting sessions across both days; session times not verified
candidates.price_text: Ticketed; price and venue not verified
candidates.summary: RAW WINE, the natural-wine fair founded by Isabelle Legeron, returns to New York on Nov 8 and 9, 2026, with a room full of small organic and biodynamic growers pouring their own wine. It is a walk-around tasting, tickets sold in advance by session.
candidates.fit: This is the natural wine fair where you talk to the person who made the bottle rather than a brand rep, which is the same reason he likes small rooms and bartenders who know things. Good date-night daytime with his wife, and it needs booking now because sessions go.

candidates.title: Resident Halloween Dinner with Chef Joshua White
candidates.time_text: Evening; exact seating time not verified
candidates.price_text: Ticketed per seat through Resident; price not verified
candidates.summary: Resident runs chef-cooked dinners in private spaces rather than restaurants. Their second annual Halloween dinner is Friday Oct 30, 2026, at Brooklyn Point in Downtown Brooklyn, hosted by Chef Joshua White, with a menu built around the styles of the chefs who shaped American cooking. Seats are sold individually in advance.
candidates.fit: A chef cooking a one-night menu in a room that is not a restaurant, with a small table of strangers, is exactly the format he keeps saying he wants, and it is fifteen minutes from Fort Greene. Halloween weekend, so it doubles as the costume-adjacent date night.

candidates.title: L'Abeille x Le Gavroche: Michel Roux Jr. residency
candidates.time_text: Dinner service; seating times not verified
candidates.price_text: Tasting-menu pricing, genuine splurge; exact price not verified
candidates.summary: Michel Roux Jr. returns to L'Abeille in Tribeca for a four-night Le Gavroche residency, Oct 13 to 16, 2026, cooking the old-guard French repertoire in a small New York dining room. Seats are limited and sold directly by the restaurant.
candidates.fit: A visiting chef cooking a one-off menu in a room of forty is the top of his list, and Tribeca is where he teaches Krav Maga anyway. This is the splurge date night for October, and it will be gone if he waits.

candidates.title: The Lovers Bar takeover at Gramercy Tavern
candidates.time_text: Evening bar service; exact hours not verified
candidates.price_text: À la carte cocktails; no cover reported, not verified
candidates.summary: Gramercy Tavern's fall guest-bar series brings out-of-town bar teams into its front room for one night each, and The Lovers Bar — the downstairs cocktail bar at Philadelphia's James Beard-winning Friday Saturday Sunday — closes the series on Oct 5, 2026. Walk-in bar room, cocktails à la carte.
candidates.fit: Same register as Raines Law Room and Overstory: serious drinks, no bottle service, no line culture, and for one night the people making them flew in. It is a Monday, so it only earns a slot if he wants a quiet, high-quality bar night.

candidates.title: Meat Asia Asian BBQ pop-up at Strong Rope Red Hook (Friday edition)
candidates.price_text: No cover; food priced per plate
candidates.summary: Meat Asia returns to Strong Rope's Red Hook taproom on Friday Oct 23, 2026, with Asian BBQ. Walk-in; the brewery takes table reservations for larger groups.
candidates.fit: The backup if Oct 3 gets rained out, and the Friday version is the better guys' slot anyway. Book a table for four rather than gambling on seats.

candidates.title: Chaat Dog pop-up at Strong Rope Red Hook
candidates.time_text: Taproom hours, Saturday afternoon into evening
candidates.price_text: No cover; food priced per plate
candidates.summary: Chaat Dog — an all-beef hot dog dressed as chaat in a ghee-toasted bun — pops up at Strong Rope Red Hook on Saturday Oct 17, 2026, alongside the El Toro Rojo truck the same day. Walk-in.
candidates.fit: He already drinks at Strong Rope; this is a reason to go on a specific Saturday with a friend and eat something stupid and good. Two vendors the same day means there is enough to make a whole afternoon of it.

candidates.title: Highball Ltd. — Jeff Bell's new hidden bar
candidates.price_text: Cocktail-bar pricing; not verified
candidates.summary: Highball Ltd. is the new bar from Jeff Bell, the bartender who ran PDT, tucked inside an office tower near Grand Central. It opened in 2026 and is built around classic drink-making rather than scene.
candidates.fit: Raines Law Room and Overstory taste, from the guy who ran PDT, and the location inside an office building means it is a bar you have to know about rather than one you walk past. Worth a look on a night he is already in Manhattan — just not a Times Square detour.

candidates.title: The Lineup Dinner — sous chefs cook their own menu
candidates.venue: The Lineup Dinner (Food52 space, Brooklyn Navy Yard)
candidates.price_text: Five courses with five wine pairings, ticketed per seat; current price not verified
candidates.summary: The Lineup is a recurring Brooklyn pop-up dinner series that hands the kitchen to a different sous chef each night, serving a five-course menu with five wines in the Food52 space in the Brooklyn Navy Yard. Seats are sold per dinner through OpenTable.
candidates.fit: Fifteen minutes from Fort Greene, one long table, and the cook is someone nobody has heard of yet — which is the whole point for him. Worth putting on alert so he can grab four seats the week a date drops.

candidates.title: Evil Trivia at Radegast Hall
candidates.price_text: No cover; food and beer à la carte
candidates.summary: Radegast Hall runs a weekly Tuesday trivia night called Evil Trivia at 7:30pm in its Williamsburg beer hall, which also has live music five nights a week with no cover. Walk-in, long communal tables, German beer and sausage.
candidates.fit: Tuesday is normally off the table, but he trains in Williamsburg, and a long communal table, liters of German beer and a trivia team of three is a low-lift version of the thing he likes. Treat it as filler, not the headline.

candidates.title: Nutcracker Rouge
candidates.summary: Company XIV's hedonistic holiday version of the Nutcracker returns to Théâtre XIV for twelve weeks. The company's own page lists previews beginning Thursday November 12, 2026, closing night Saturday January 30, 2027, and all tickets on sale now. Adults only.
candidates.fit: He loves the Nutcracker at Lincoln Center and he loves Company XIV; this is both at once, in his borough. Book now, because the good seats and the champagne couches go first and December weekends disappear.

candidates.title: Rocky Horror Picture Show with The Occasionalists
candidates.summary: A screening of Rocky Horror with The Occasionalists shadow cast performing live in front of the film, the night before Halloween at Littlefield. Listed on Littlefield's own calendar for October 30, 7:30pm to 10:30pm. Costumes and audience participation are the whole point.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for Rocky Horror in Flatbush and had a great time; this is the same thing with a proper shadow cast, in a 200-cap room ten minutes from home, on the Friday of Halloween weekend.

candidates.title: The 24th Annual New York Burlesque Festival
candidates.price_text: $55-$75 for the Sony Hall night; 3-day Crystal VIP pass $240
candidates.summary: Thirsty Girl Productions' 24th edition runs October 2 to 4, 2026 across Sony Hall, 3 Dollar Bill in Bushwick and Le Poisson Rouge, with dozens of burlesque performers flown in from around the world. Ticketmaster lists the Saturday show at Sony Hall on October 3 at 7pm; the festival's VIP pass is $240.
candidates.fit: This is the annual gathering of the scene Company XIV plays in, and the Bushwick night at 3 Dollar Bill is the one with the real crowd rather than the Midtown room. Pick a single night rather than the pass.

candidates.title: Nick Mestad: Body Of Work
candidates.summary: Nick Mestad headlines the Union Hall basement with Devon Walker, Jack Bensinger, Jo Sunday and Camden Garcia on the bill. Union Hall's own calendar lists it for Thursday October 1. The room seats under 150 with a bar upstairs before and after.
candidates.fit: This is his Thursday slot: a sub-150-seat basement, a lineup of working New York comics rather than an arena name, and a bar you can keep sitting in afterward with one or two friends.

candidates.title: Whiplash
candidates.summary: Whiplash, the long-running New York stand-up showcase, lands at Union Hall on Friday October 2 with Shalewa Sharpe, Jay Jurden, Julia Shiplett and Liza Treyger. Confirmed on Union Hall's calendar; tickets through Eventbrite.
candidates.fit: Four genuinely good club comics in a basement instead of one comedian in an arena, which is the trade he keeps saying he wants. Easy Friday plan for two or three of the guys.

candidates.title: Daylighters (A Comedy Show You Can Bring Your Kids To)
candidates.summary: An afternoon stand-up show at Littlefield explicitly built so parents can bring the kid along, listed on Littlefield's calendar for Sunday October 4, 3pm to 4:30pm. Real venue, real comics, daylight hours, done well before dinner.
candidates.fit: The family pick that doesn't bore the adults: a stroller-friendly Sunday afternoon in a real Gowanus venue rather than another lap of Fort Greene Park, and it's over by 4:30.

candidates.title: The George Lucas Talk Show
candidates.summary: The cult live talk show where a man plays George Lucas and interviews real guests, staged at Littlefield on Thursday October 8 at 8pm with guests to be announced. It has a devoted, loud, in-on-it audience and is a Brooklyn comedy institution rather than a touring product.
candidates.fit: Exactly the 'you had to know about it' comedy he wants, on a Thursday, in a small Gowanus room. Bring the friend who will get every joke.

candidates.title: Switch n' Play Presents: Slash n' Spray
candidates.summary: Switch n' Play, Brooklyn's veteran drag and burlesque collective, brings a Halloween-season edition called Slash n' Spray to Littlefield on Saturday October 24, 8pm to 10pm. It is a rotating cast of drag kings, queens and burlesque performers with a crowd that knows every performer by name.
candidates.fit: He goes to drag shows at Phoenix with the guys; Switch n' Play is the smarter, weirder Brooklyn version of that, and a horror-themed October edition is the right night to bring people to.

candidates.title: NYC's Halloween Punderdome
candidates.summary: Punderdome is Brooklyn's long-running competitive punning gameshow, judged by audience noise, and the Halloween edition on Wednesday October 28 adds a pun-costume competition. Listed on Littlefield's calendar, 8pm to 10:30pm. Anyone can throw their name in the hat to compete.
candidates.fit: Interactive in the way he actually likes: you can get on stage, there's a costume angle, and it's a home-grown Brooklyn institution with no marketing budget. It's a Wednesday, so only worth it if the crew is up for a costume.

candidates.title: House of Hallucinations
candidates.summary: House of Yes's flagship Halloween production, listed on aggregator calendars for Friday October 30 and Saturday October 31 at around 10pm. Expect aerial and circus acts, a full costume mandate and a late dance floor in the Bushwick warehouse.
candidates.fit: His once-in-a-while spectacle night, and the Halloween one is the only House of Yes booking that justifies the crowd. Costumes, performers overhead, dancing until late, and a car home to Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Steve Martin Presents with Andrew Dismukes and Michael Good
candidates.summary: A stand-up showcase billed as Steve Martin Presents with Andrew Dismukes and Michael Good, listed on Union Hall's calendar for Sunday October 4. Union Hall's basement is a sub-150 seat room. Tickets via Eventbrite.
candidates.fit: A Sunday-night, low-commitment version of his small-room comedy habit, with an SNL cast member working out material in a basement in Park Slope.

candidates.title: Hoodo Hersi: Extraordinary Alien
candidates.summary: Comedian Hoodo Hersi performs her show Extraordinary Alien at Union Hall on Saturday October 3, per Union Hall's own calendar. It's a single-comic hour in the basement room rather than a showcase.
candidates.fit: If he'd rather see one comic build an actual hour than a parade of ten-minute sets, this is the Saturday version, and Union Hall's bar is a fine place to sit before and after with the guys.

candidates.title: Mr. Choade's Upstairs Downstairs
candidates.time_text: evening show, with a separate midnight show the same night
candidates.summary: The Slipper Room's signature variety show, a mix of burlesque, sideshow, magic and comedy hosted in their 1890s-style room on Orchard Street, is listed on the venue's calendar for Saturday October 3, with a Slipper Room Midnight Show the same night. The venue has been running variety on this block since 1999. Ticket price was not confirmed.
candidates.fit: Hidden-door Lower East Side variety in a room where you can talk to the bartender between acts, which is the same register as Sunken Harbor Club but with tassels. Good late option after dinner downtown with his wife.

candidates.title: Karaoke Tremendous
candidates.price_text: free RSVP
candidates.summary: Union Hall's recurring karaoke night, listed on the venue's calendar for Friday October 2 with a free Eventbrite registration rather than a paid ticket. It runs in the basement performance room, so it's a stage and a crowd rather than a private booth.
candidates.fit: He likes karaoke leagues and bars doing weird programming, and this is the participation version: sign up, sing, no cover. Cheap Friday plan that still counts as a plan.

candidates.title: Joke Machine with Emmy Blotnick & Joe Zimmerman
candidates.summary: Joke Machine, hosted by Emmy Blotnick and Joe Zimmerman, with Brittany Carney and Brendan Scannell on the bill, at Union Hall on Wednesday September 30 per the venue's calendar. It's a joke-focused showcase in the basement room.
candidates.fit: Only here because the lineup is unusually good for a midweek basement show; if a Wednesday is doable, it's a better hour than anything on television.

candidates.title: Scary Good Comedy with Brittany Carney
candidates.summary: A Halloween-night stand-up show hosted by Brittany Carney at Littlefield, listed on the venue's calendar for Saturday October 31, 7:30pm to 10pm. Early enough that you can go somewhere in costume afterward.
candidates.fit: A Halloween plan for the group that isn't standing in a nightclub line: comedy first in Gowanus, then walk into whatever party comes next still sober enough to enjoy it.

candidates.title: Demi Adejuyigbe Sells Out
candidates.summary: Part of the New York Comedy Festival, Demi Adejuyigbe plays two shows at Littlefield on Monday November 9, at 7pm and 9:30pm, per the venue's calendar. He's the internet-native comedy writer and performer whose live shows are built around bits you cannot get anywhere else.
candidates.fit: This is a book-now, not a maybe: his shows sell out fast and the 200-cap room is the reason to go. Monday is the price of admission.

candidates.title: Bushwick Film Festival 2026
candidates.price_text: passes listed from $60 to $495; individual screenings sold separately
candidates.summary: The 19th Bushwick Film Festival runs October 7 to 11, 2026 across Brooklyn venues, with opening night at Lot 45 on Wednesday October 7 from 6:30 to 11pm and filmmakers and industry guests in the room. Passes are listed from $60 to $495.
candidates.fit: Neighborhood film festival where the director is standing at the bar afterward, which is the opposite of a listicle event. Thursday and Friday screenings plus the parties are the part worth showing up for.

candidates.title: Stand-up at The Tiny Cupboard
candidates.time_text: shows most nights, typically early and late evening
candidates.price_text: usually $5 to $10
candidates.summary: An indie comedy club in Bushwick, founded by Amy Wong and Matt Rosenblum, that grew out of a 153-square-foot art studio into a rooftop room and now a club with a board-game bar and screening space behind it. Shows run nearly every night, usually $5 to $10, with no drink minimum, mixing local up-and-comers with TV-credit comics.
candidates.fit: The closest thing in the city to that apartment comedy show he loved: tiny room, cheap, no drink minimum, and you're two feet from the comic. Good default when a Thursday opens up with no notice.

candidates.title: Don't Tell Comedy (secret-location shows)
candidates.time_text: most shows start around 7pm or 8:30pm; address emailed at 8am the day of the show
candidates.neighborhood: varies, including Williamsburg, Bushwick and Fort Greene
candidates.summary: Don't Tell Comedy runs stand-up shows in apartments, backyards, studios and small businesses across Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan. You buy by neighborhood and get the exact address by email at 8am on the day of the show; lineups are unannounced and often include comics with real credits. New dates post continuously, so check the New York page for the week you want.
candidates.fit: He once went to a random apartment comedy show in Midtown and loved it; this is that format, bookable, in his own neighborhoods. Perfect for a Thursday when he wants to hand friends an address they can't Google.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Atlantic Ave day pass
candidates.time_text: open daily, roughly 8am to 11:30pm; book a slot, stay as long as you want
candidates.price_text: from $29, varies by day and time
candidates.summary: Bathhouse's newest Brooklyn location opened in 2026 at 540 Atlantic Ave, a few minutes from Barclays Center. Three thermal pools (104F hot, 50F cold plunge, 98F neutral), a banya running 185-195F, steam rooms, and an Event Sauna up to 175F with complimentary Aufguss ceremonies during your visit. Day passes start at $29 and prices float with day and time; single entry, no re-entry.
candidates.fit: The full bathhouse day with a friend is one of his favorite things, and this one is a walk from Fort Greene instead of a train to the East Village. Book a late Thursday slot with one of the guys and you are home by eleven.

candidates.title: World Spa full day in the Grand Banya
candidates.time_text: all-day access; give it four hours minimum
candidates.price_text: day passes from $99
candidates.summary: A 50,000 sq ft bathhouse in Borough Park with 16 thermal rooms: the largest banya in the US (176-194F, venik birch-branch beatings included in the ritual), a petite banya, Moroccan and Turkish hammams, onsen pools, a snow room, salt room, cold plunge and an Event Sauna where sauna masters run Aufguss. Day passes start at $99 and there is a restaurant and lounge so you can stay all day.
candidates.fit: This is the upgrade on the Russian & Turkish Baths day he loved: same venik-and-plunge ritual, ten times the building, and a restaurant so a five-hour Saturday with a friend actually works.

candidates.title: TWA Hotel rooftop pool before the season rule changes
candidates.time_text: non-hotel guests 11am to 11pm; reservations are 1 hour 45 minutes
candidates.address: One Idlewild Drive, JFK Airport, Queens, NY 11430
candidates.price_text: from $50 adults, $10 kids 5-12, under 5 free
candidates.summary: The rooftop infinity pool over JFK's runway 4L/22R is open year round and heated to 95 degrees in cold months. Non-hotel guests book through ResortPass: cover starts at $50 for adults, $10 for kids 5-12, free under 5, and includes the observation deck and towels. Reservations are required through November 1 and each slot runs 1 hour 45 minutes; note the rooftop is closed for a private event on Sept 29 from 6pm to 9pm.
candidates.fit: He has done this one and loved it, and the 95-degree winter pool-cuzzi version is the move nobody thinks of in October. Toddler swims free and spends an hour pointing at 747s, which makes it a real family morning rather than a playground.

candidates.title: NYC Century Bike Tour
candidates.summary: Transportation Alternatives is bringing back the NYC Century on October 25, 2026 after a six-year gap. It is the only all-urban century in the country, with 40, 55, 75 and 100-mile route choices through the boroughs, and the listing includes a rain guarantee that reimburses your registration fee up to $100 if half an inch falls at the Central Park gauge.
candidates.fit: He rode Lower Manhattan to the GW Bridge with friends and called it a highlight; this is that ride with rest stops, cue sheets and 40/55/75 options so the group can pick its own suffering. Registration tiers climb as the date gets closer, so lock it in now.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Williamsburg rooftop pool and day pass
candidates.price_text: from $39, varies by day and time
candidates.summary: The Williamsburg flagship runs saunas, steam rooms, hot and cold plunges and a rooftop pool. Rooftop access comes with any day pass, massage or scrub on a first-come mixed-seating basis; daybeds and lounge chairs are booked separately and open up ten days out. Day passes start at $39 and Bathhouse sells rooftop access only through its own site, never a third party.
candidates.fit: He trains Muay Thai in Williamsburg, so this is a post-session plunge that doesn't cost a separate trip, and the rooftop is still usable in early October if the weather holds.

candidates.title: QC NY on Governors Island, autumn season
candidates.time_text: Sun-Thu 9am to 10pm, Fri-Sat 9am to 11pm; ferry runs until 10pm weekdays, 11pm weekends
candidates.address: 112 Andes Road, Governors Island, New York, NY 10004
candidates.summary: QC's spa in the restored officers' housing on Governors Island has heated outdoor courtyard pools, timber saunas, steam rooms and 20-plus wellness stations, and it is currently running autumn programming with fall foliage, outdoor fires and Aperitivo evenings with wine and charcuterie. Entry includes robe, towels and slippers; you get there by ferry, which is half the appeal. Admission prices vary by day and are listed on their prices page.
candidates.fit: Date night that starts with a boat: ferry over, heated pools with the skyline going dark at 6pm, aperitivo in a robe. Same register as the Russian baths day but polished enough for his wife, and it is not a place everyone in Fort Greene has already been.

candidates.title: Beat Drop DJ Takeover at Othership Williamsburg
candidates.time_text: evening sessions, about two hours end to end
candidates.summary: Othership's Williamsburg location (185F performance sauna, eight ice baths between 32F and 39F, amphitheater tea lounge) runs Beat Drop, a roughly two-hour guided sauna session with a live DJ takeover instead of the usual soundtrack. It is a booked class, not a drop-in, and it runs on a rotating schedule rather than a fixed night. Check the schedule page for the next Williamsburg date and price.
candidates.fit: Sauna with an actual DJ is the overlap of two things he already does, and it is guided rather than a room full of people scrolling. Worth one shot to see whether the DJ is playing real melodic house or spa ambience with a BPM.

candidates.title: Aufguss sauna ceremony at Bathhouse
candidates.time_text: hosted daily at every location; about 15 minutes per ceremony
candidates.price_text: included with a day pass from $29
candidates.summary: Aufguss is the German sauna ritual: a sauna master works the room with essential oils, music and choreographed towel waving to push waves of heat over you, about 15 minutes a round. Bathhouse runs them daily at all four locations, including the Event Sauna on Atlantic Ave, and they are included in the price of a day pass. Times are posted on the schedule each day.
candidates.fit: A German ritual, performed, in a small hot room, included in the $29 he was paying anyway. Time the Atlantic Ave booking around a ceremony and it stops being a sauna visit and becomes a thing you drag a friend to.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Bathhouse at Night (monthly DJ party)
candidates.summary: Brooklyn Bathhouse runs a monthly Friday night party where the ticket covers saunas, steam room, hot and cold plunges and relaxation spaces plus local DJ sets, a complimentary mocktail and a full bar with food for purchase. Confirmed editions ran June 19, July 24 and August 21, 2026, and an edition billed as the Pink Edition is listed on Eventbrite. The next date is not confirmed, so search the organizer on Eventbrite before making plans.
candidates.fit: Small-room, word-of-mouth, cold plunge with a DJ and a bar: exactly the register he wants and the opposite of a spa day. Treat this as a lead to check, not a booked plan.

candidates.title: Tammam Azzam: A Horizon Remains
candidates.time_text: during gallery hours; check the site before you go
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: The Goethe-Institut's New York space is showing the first solo exhibition and US institutional presentation of Syrian-German artist Tammam Azzam, running September 16 through December 3, 2026. Admission is free. It is a small institutional gallery, not a museum blockbuster.
candidates.fit: It is the German cultural institute, free, and small enough to do in forty minutes before dinner - the kind of thing you walk into because you knew it was there, not because it topped a list. Pairs well with a weeknight drink for him and his wife.

candidates.title: Too Much Is Better Than Too Little: Alfred Hilsberg, ZickZack & the Invention of the German Underground
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: A Goethe-Institut New York project on Alfred Hilsberg, the ZickZack label and the German post-punk underground of the late 70s and 80s, running October 8 to November 7, 2026, free, in English. The Goethe events page also lists companion talks on the German home-recording tape scene 1980-1990 with Felix Kubin and on East German punk on record, tape and celluloid; dates for those talks were not posted where I could read them.
candidates.fit: This is the origin story of the German music he actually listens to - the underground that ran from Neue Deutsche Welle to the Berlin stuff he still plays. A free exhibition plus a Felix Kubin talk is exactly the Berlin-adjacent deep scene he wants more of.

candidates.title: Kafka's Drawings: Images of the Grotesque and Arabesque
candidates.summary: A Deutsches Haus at NYU lecture on Kafka's drawings, Tuesday October 6, 6:00 to 7:30pm, at 42 Washington Mews. Deutsches Haus programming is generally free with advance RSVP; I could not open the registration page to confirm price or capacity.
candidates.fit: Small German-speaking-world institution, no marketing budget, thirty people in a townhouse off Washington Square. It is a Tuesday, so it is radar rather than a group plan - but it is the kind of German cultural room he keeps asking for.

candidates.title: Festival Neue Literatur 2026
candidates.summary: New York's festival of new German-language literature runs two evenings at Deutsches Haus at NYU: "Intimate Thresholds: Identity and Longing" on Monday October 26 and "Guests and Ghosts" on Tuesday October 27, both 6:00 to 7:30pm at 42 Washington Mews. Full author line-ups and RSVP details were on pages I could not open.
candidates.fit: The one week a year that German, Austrian and Swiss writers are actually in New York, in a forty-person room rather than a bookstore basement. Worth putting on the calendar now even though both nights are early-week.

candidates.title: Rabih Mroué & Lina Majdalanie: Four Walls and a Roof
candidates.summary: North American premiere of a theater piece by Rabih Mroué and Lina Majdalanie, October 22 to 24, 2026, at NYU Skirball, supported by the Goethe-Institut. Show times and ticket prices are on the Skirball page, which I could not load.
candidates.fit: He does not want generic theater, but a North American premiere by two artists who mostly show in Berlin and Beirut is the other thing entirely - a date night where the conversation afterwards is the point.

candidates.title: Oktoberfest Saturdays at Radegast Hall & Biergarten
candidates.summary: Radegast runs its Oktoberfest on consecutive Saturdays through early October with brass bands, keg tapping and steins. October 3 is also German Unity Day. I could not get onto Radegast's own site to confirm the 2026 Saturday dates or times, and the listings I found disagree with each other.
candidates.fit: It is the beer hall five minutes from Kings Combat, it is a real German room rather than a lederhosen frat party, and October 3 is the German national holiday - a good excuse to pull two or three guys out on a Saturday afternoon. Call the hall first; the date is not confirmed.

candidates.title: Zum Stammtisch
candidates.time_text: kitchen open from midday most days; closed Mondays
candidates.summary: A German restaurant and bar in Glendale, Queens, open since 1972 and essentially unchanged: wurst plates, schnitzel, liter steins, dirndls, taxidermy on the walls. There is a beer shop next door. No reservations system worth gaming and no line culture.
candidates.fit: This is the German room that is actually German - the opposite of a Midtown beer garden. A table of four, a wurst plate each and a stein is a complete guys' night, and it is the right register for someone who plays Lichterkinder in the car.

candidates.title: Barbès
candidates.time_text: music most nights from around 7pm; weekends open from 2pm
candidates.price_text: most shows are a door charge or donation, roughly $10 to $20
candidates.summary: A bar and back room in Park Slope that has presented music nightly for 24 years - klezmer, Balkan brass, chicha, West African and Latin bands - in a room that holds well under a hundred people. Shows are door-charge or donation, paid online in advance or at the door. The current month's calendar is a downloadable PDF on their events page.
candidates.fit: He asked for klezmer in a small room; this is the small room, and it is a fifteen-minute drive from Fort Greene. No listings site covers it properly, which is exactly why it qualifies as something you had to know about.

candidates.title: Governors Island ferry day
candidates.time_text: ferries run through the day; go in the morning and be back for a nap
candidates.price_text: ferry fare; check the site for current pricing and free windows
candidates.summary: A short ferry to a car-free island with lawns, food vendors and hammocks, reachable from Brooklyn Bridge Park as well as the Battery Maritime Building. Open year round. I could not load the current schedule and fare page to confirm October ferry times.
candidates.fit: A ferry ride with an actual destination is the family format that works: the boat is the event for the 1-year-old, the island is stroller-flat, and he and his wife get a morning that feels like leaving town without leaving the five boroughs. Check the October ferry schedule before you commit.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Children's Museum weekend morning
candidates.summary: The Crown Heights children's museum runs weekend programming including sessions aimed at the youngest visitors. I could not load the October event calendar to confirm which weekend programs are running or what they cost.
candidates.fit: Crown Heights is already his territory, it is indoors if the weather turns, and it is done by lunch. This is the fallback family pick, not the exciting one - check their calendar for a specific weekend program before you go.

candidates.title: Lost Miracle: Sébastien Léger x Roy Rosenfeld
candidates.price_text: from $30 on Dice
candidates.summary: Sébastien Léger brings his Lost Miracle label showcase back to New York with Roy Rosenfeld, in the open-air Ruins at Knockdown Center on Friday October 2. Tickets start around $30 on Dice. Léger founded Lost Miracle in 2019 and the series is built around long, story-driven melodic sets rather than peak-time bangers.
candidates.fit: This is the deadmau5/Eric Prydz/Tinlicker lane done properly: melodic, progressive, played long-form in a room that is not an arena. It is also a Friday, which is one of his slots.

candidates.title: Jordan Nocturne + Arvin T (Bad Room: Laila Amira, Lady Harley)
candidates.price_text: advance tickets on RA; price not listed on the venue calendar
candidates.summary: Belfast's Jordan Nocturne headlines Good Room's main room on Saturday October 3 with Arvin T opening, while Laila Amira and Lady Harley play the Bad Room all night. Advance tickets are on Resident Advisor via the venue calendar. Good Room is a two-room Greenpoint club, not a big box.
candidates.fit: Small room, serious sound, a DJ who actually plays a set — his stated preference over a mediocre arena show. Good Room is the kind of place you have to already know about.

candidates.title: LockedIn Auto Club x Nowadays Creative Lab: GET LICENSED
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: LockedIn Auto Club takes over Nowadays Creative Lab on Friday October 2, 5pm to 8pm: get a headshot taken and printed onto a free LockedIn t-shirt while a curated lineup of cars from Daikoku NYC and Gearheads NYC sits outside. Drinks for sale from Clientele Cafe, food from 7th Street Burger. Free, while shirts last.
candidates.fit: He named Daikoku NYC as the deep car scene he wants more of, and this is Daikoku cars plus an interactive thing you leave holding. It is 5-8pm on a Friday, so it slots in before a late set.

candidates.title: The FreakShow 4 Year Anniversary: The Roast of Siobhan the Third
candidates.time_text: night; door time not stated in the announcement
candidates.summary: The FreakShow, All Night Skate's long-running drag and variety night, turns four on Thursday October 1 with a full roast of host Siobhan the Third, a stacked guest list of performers and DJ mt.aloofa on the decks. Announced on the host's Instagram; no ticket link was posted, so treat it as a show-up-and-pay-at-the-bar night.
candidates.fit: He already loves All Night Skate and drag shows with the guys, and this is the bar's own scene night on his main weeknight slot. Roast format means it is loose, mean and not a tourist room.

candidates.title: SundaySunday: Axel Boman, Rebolledo
candidates.price_text: $28 on Dice
candidates.summary: Mexico City's SundaySunday party takes over The Ruins on October 4 with Swedish house oddball Axel Boman, Rebolledo and the party's residents. Tickets are listed at $27.87 on Dice. It is the crew's first Brooklyn edition.
candidates.fit: An imported party with residents nobody here has seen yet, in the open-air Ruins rather than a club — the 'you had to know about it' end of the house scene he wants.

candidates.title: Petite Rouge
candidates.summary: Company XIV's burlesque-ballet retelling of Little Red Riding Hood closes October 31, with the company posting that only six weekends remain and that spooky-season upgrades are available. Tickets and seating tiers through Company XIV's site. Théâtre XIV seats a few hundred with cocktail service at the tables.
candidates.fit: Company XIV is already a favorite and their Halloween-season show was a highlight — this is the same room, the same register, and it disappears on November 1. Book the babysitter.

candidates.title: Tootsie's Video Vault 7
candidates.summary: A short-film race in its sixth year: NYC filmmakers get three months to make a three-minute short, and all of them screen in one night at littlefield on Saturday October 3. Awards include Best Actor, Best Director and joke superlatives, and audience members are eligible for prizes like Best Dressed. Tickets on Eventbrite via littlefield.
candidates.fit: Community-run, no marketing budget, audience is part of the show — the opposite of a listicle night out, and littlefield is a 10-minute drive from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Tiny Table Tennis Tournament
candidates.price_text: sign-up fee not posted; cash prize for winners
candidates.summary: The Tiny Cupboard runs its recurring ping pong tournament on Sunday October 4, casual bracket at 1pm and pro bracket at 3pm, with a cash prize for winners. Sign-ups are through crystal-clear link in the venue's bio; the flyer did not list an entry fee.
candidates.fit: Interactive, competitive, Sunday daytime, and run out of a tiny comedy bar in Bushwick rather than a sports bar. Bring one friend and enter the casual bracket.

candidates.title: Lobster Place takeover of the Threes Gowanus Yard
candidates.price_text: free to attend, food and drink priced separately
candidates.summary: Lobster Place takes over the Threes Brewing yard in Gowanus on Thursday October 1, 5pm to 9pm, with grilled and chilled seafood and drink specials. One night only, RSVP through the link in Threes' bio. Threes is also pouring $15 steins of its Hereafter Oktoberfest lager this season.
candidates.fit: A one-night guest takeover in a beer yard on a Thursday — his favorite food format (visiting kitchen, shared table, outdoors) without a reservation war.

candidates.title: FALSA
candidates.summary: Falsa plays Barbès on Saturday October 3 at 8pm with a lineup including Sunny Jain on drums, Kenny Warren on trumpet, Roshni Samlal on tabla and Umer Piracha on vocals — Sufi repertoire taken apart and rebuilt through improvisation. The band posted a ticket link (tinyurl.com/oct3falsa); Barbès' back room holds well under 100 people.
candidates.fit: A 60-seat back room where you are three feet from the players is precisely his small-room standard, and Barbès is the word-of-mouth institution he should be using more.

candidates.title: NEW MOON: a Twilight party at Phoenix
candidates.price_text: free, no cover
candidates.summary: Talia Fortune's First Fridays at Phoenix goes full Twilight on Friday October 2: movies on the TVs all night, pop-up performances, trivia and $100 cash for the best vampire or werewolf costume. No cover, 10pm until late.
candidates.fit: He already goes to Phoenix for drag nights with friends, and this is the costume-and-theme format he actually enjoys (see: the ABBA night, Rocky Horror) for the price of the drinks.

candidates.title: Art of Manga opening weekend
candidates.price_text: Manga Fan Pass $75 covers one adult plus a guest for the run; standard timed tickets sold separately
candidates.summary: The Brooklyn Museum opens Art of Manga on October 3, with original artwork from Araki Hirohiko, Oda Eiichiro, Takahashi Rumiko, Taniguchi Jirō and others, laid out right-to-left like a manga page. Cosplay is encouraged. Advance timed tickets through the museum; a $75 Manga Fan Pass gives two people unlimited entry for the run.
candidates.fit: Weekend-daytime, stroller-friendly, ten minutes from Fort Greene, and genuinely interesting to the adults — the family slot without defaulting to a playground.

candidates.title: 718 Sessions Holiday Party with Danny Krivit
candidates.price_text: $5 for the first 100 before 7pm, $15 to $25 advance on RA, $20 with a flyer at the door, $30 without
candidates.summary: Danny Krivit's 718 Sessions lands at Good Room on Sunday October 11 with doors at 6pm, That Matt in the Bad Room and lights by Ariel. Columbus Day Monday means it runs late without wrecking the week. Advance tickets $15 to $25 on Resident Advisor.
candidates.fit: A 40-year New York DJ institution in a 250-capacity room, starting at 6pm — the deep-scene, dance-to-a-real-selector night that never shows up on a listicle.

candidates.title: Ahmed Spins, Sapian, Mehdi
candidates.price_text: from $38 on Dice
candidates.summary: South African Afro-house producer Ahmed Spins makes his Main Hall debut at Knockdown Center on Saturday October 24 after selling out The Ruins in May, joined by Sapian and Deep House Bible's Mehdi. Tickets from $38 on Dice and the venue says stock is limited.
candidates.fit: Sits exactly between his two current lanes — melodic house and the South African/Afro sound he has been adding all year. Buy now; the Ruins show sold out.

candidates.title: Honey Dijon: Day & Night
candidates.time_text: day into night, open to close
candidates.price_text: from $48 on Dice
candidates.summary: Honey Dijon plays a day-and-night marathon at Knockdown Center on Saturday October 10, listed on Dice from $48.47. The Day & Night format means one DJ across the whole session rather than a rotating lineup.
candidates.fit: You can show up at 4pm, dance in daylight and be out before it turns into a 4am situation — the dad-friendly version of a big Brooklyn warehouse night.

candidates.title: Dreamland presents Armin van Buuren
candidates.summary: Armin van Buuren returns to Brooklyn Storehouse on Friday October 9 for a special extended set, announced by the venue with tickets on sale now via their link in bio. It is one of the last shows of Storehouse's closing season. The venue did not post a price.
candidates.fit: Filed under his 2016-era big-room nostalgia: this is the once-in-a-while spectacle, in a warehouse rather than a stadium, with an extended set instead of a 60-minute festival slot.

candidates.title: The Blaze (live)
candidates.summary: French duo The Blaze play a special live set in Knockdown Center's Main Hall on Wednesday October 28. Artist presale is Wednesday September 30 at noon ET; public on-sale Friday October 2 at noon ET, sign-up through the venue's link in bio. Their last release, Folk, was a live album recorded at the Royal Albert Hall.
candidates.fit: Cinematic live electronic music rather than a DJ set — the Polo & Pan / Empire of the Sun side of his library, and the kind of show that sells out the hour it goes up. Mid-week, so only if he wants it badly.

candidates.title: Dax J — all night long (open to close)
candidates.summary: Berlin-based techno DJ Dax J plays his first ever open-to-close set in the US at Knockdown Center on Saturday November 14, announced on his own Instagram with presale sign-up and general sale following. Listed on Resident Advisor's Knockdown Center page for 14 Nov.
candidates.fit: Berlin techno, one DJ, all night, in a warehouse — the Kalkbrenner/Berghain end of his taste, and a 'sometimes thing' worth planning a late night around.

candidates.title: Too Much Is Better Than Too Little: Alfred Hilsberg, ZickZack & the Invention of the German Underground — opening
candidates.summary: The first exhibition outside Germany on punk journalist and ZickZack label founder Alfred Hilsberg, curated by Sukhdev Sandhu and presented with Goethe-Institut New York. Opening reception Thursday October 8, 6 to 8pm; the show runs through November 7 and includes photography, Super-8 films and rare records. The gallery did not list an address in the post.
candidates.fit: German underground culture as an actual art opening with a crowd, not a lecture — hits both the Berlin streak and the 'art opening that is really a party' thing he liked at the photo studio.

candidates.title: Meshuganah Mambo
candidates.summary: Klezmer meets tropical dance music at Barbès on Friday October 9 at 8pm, with a band of percussion, organ, sax, drums and bass playing for dancing. Posted by the bandleader; Barbès runs on a suggested contribution at the door rather than advance tickets.
candidates.fit: Klezmer in a tiny room is literally on his list, and this version is a dance party rather than a concert. Cheap, weird, and nobody he knows will have heard of it.

candidates.title: Synthicide Halloween: Terence Fixmer, Andi
candidates.summary: Good Room's Halloween is Synthicide's annual party on Friday October 30, headlined by French EBM/techno producer Terence Fixmer with Andi, plus Justin Aulis Long and Stiffdance in the Bad Room. Tickets on Resident Advisor via the venue calendar.
candidates.fit: A costume night with actual Berlin-adjacent body music instead of a DJ playing Monster Mash — the correct Halloween for someone whose Tier 1 includes Kalkbrenner and Rebūke.

candidates.title: JJQ and the Q Brothers: improvised hip-hop for the whole family
candidates.summary: The Q Brothers bring their improvised hip-hop show plus a DJ set to Brooklyn Bowl at 11:45am on Saturday October 24, all ages, kids encouraged. Announced by the performers; tickets through Brooklyn Bowl.
candidates.fit: A late-morning kids' show that is actually a hip-hop set in a real venue — the family pick that does not punish the adults, and he can be back in Fort Greene by nap time.

candidates.title: PRELUDE by En Garde Arts (Anne Bogart & Charles L. Mee)
candidates.time_text: outdoor performance; show times posted on BAM's event page
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: En Garde Arts stages PRELUDE, a large-scale free outdoor performance on the BAM plaza at 300 Ashland Place, October 13 to 15, reuniting director Anne Bogart and playwright Charles L. Mee with original music by the Lazours and costumes by Machine Dazzle. Free and outdoors; BAM did not post start times in the announcement.
candidates.fit: It is free, it is strange, and it is on the plaza he walks past every day — a no-commitment culture night in his front yard, and workable with the kid in a carrier if the timing lands in daylight.

laneReports.notes:
Verification status: everything sourced from publicrecords.nyc and elsewhere.club was read directly off the organizer calendars, both retrieved on 2026-09-28, so dates, rooms and start times are solid. Neither calendar publishes prices in the page text, so price_text is mostly empty — prices are on the linked Dice/Eventbrite pages and I could not open them before running out of tool budget. Circoloco (Brooklyn Storehouse, Oct 30–31, billed as the venue's closing nights) was confirmed on a detailed doNYC event page with full lineup and the official circolocoibiza.com ticket link, but not on the promoter page itself. Mister Sunday at Nowadays on Oct 4 (3–9pm, set times 3–6 Justin, 6–8 Eamon) came from the RA event page content via search, not a direct page read. Kruder & Dorfmeister at Brooklyn Steel Oct 1, Ahmed Spins at Knockdown Oct 24 (~$38 on Dice), KETTAMA at Knockdown Oct 9 and Bound: Blackout at Basement Oct 30 are all single-source listings — have him confirm on the venue page before buying.

Sources that failed: ra.co geolocated my requests to Columbus, Ohio and returned no New York listings at all, and RA club pages render client-side so they came back empty — that knocked out the single best listing source for this lane. knockdown.center/upcoming, goodroombk.com, basementny.net and the Dice venue pages all returned fetch errors.
